critical_code_review_comments: server.py admin_purge_seed_data does 6 separate DELETE round-trips against Supabase without wrapping in a transaction. If any deliverables/invoices delete fails mid-flight, you're left with orphan review_threads / partial state and no rollback. Consider a Postgres RPC (`purge_seed_data()`) that runs in a single transaction with FK CASCADE.

auth deletion loop calls sb.auth.admin.delete_user() then sb.table('clients').delete().eq('id', c['id']) in sequence per client — no batching, no retry. For 3 clients this is fine, but at scale (say 1000 tagged clients) that's 2000+ round-trips. Batch the clients delete after the auth loop, or use RPC.

Order of deletion inside the loop is: auth delete → clients row delete. If auth deletion succeeds but the subsequent clients delete fails (network blip), you get an orphaned clients row pointing at a deleted user_id — recovery is manual. Swap the order (delete clients row first) or wrap in try/except that re-queues.

auth_users_failed_review_manually is returned but the clients row is STILL deleted even when the auth deletion errored (line 478 runs unconditionally after the try/except). This is the opposite of what the field name implies — the caller would assume 'review manually' means the record was preserved. Either preserve the clients row on auth-delete failure, or rename the field to auth_delete_errors_but_record_still_deleted.

Admin.js purgeSeed relies on window.prompt — this is blocked/coerced-to-null in some enterprise browsers and can't be styled. Consider a proper confirmation modal with a typed input for parity with the rest of the shadcn UI (and it would be easier to e2e-test without the fragile page.on('dialog') hack).
